events.headline: Democrats Retake Senate and House in US Midterms; Trump Vows No Policy Change
events.summary: Democrats flipped at least seven Senate seats and retook the House, with Keisha Lance Bottoms winning Georgia's governorship and Deb Haaland winning New Mexico. Wall Street rallied on the results. President Trump said he would not alter his agenda despite the losses.

events.headline: El Salvador's Haiti Troop Deployment Expands as UN Confirms Gang Leader's Peace Letter
events.summary: El Salvador has deployed over 2,000 troops to Haiti, and the UN confirmed receipt of a peace letter from a Haitian gang leader. New election dates have also been announced amid the ongoing security crisis in Port-au-Prince.

events.headline: Urda Rail Crash Probe Focuses on Signal-Override Order From Madrid Control Centre
events.summary: Investigators probing the Oct 28 high-speed rail collision near Urda (at least 68-69 killed) say that after a computer failure disabled the automatic safety system, an operator at Adif's Madrid-Atocha control centre told the AVE driver to resume normal running despite a red signal, even though the other train had reported it was still stopped on the track. Spain's rail accident authority has widened the investigation.

events.headline: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Cases Top 10,500 With Death Toll Still Rising
events.summary: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo's Ituri province has surpassed 10,500 cases, with the case-fatality rate remaining above 50%. US and international health agencies continue scenario assessments as the outbreak's cross-border spread remains a concern.

events.headline: Russian Strike Death Toll in Komyshuvakha Aid Site Attack Rises to Nearly 40
events.summary: The death toll from a Russian strike on an aid distribution site and shelter in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, has risen to 37-40 people as search operations enter a third day. Ukrainian officials say the figure may still climb.

events.headline: US Strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Tankers Catch Fire in Strait of Hormuz
events.summary: The US carried out further strikes on targets near Iran's Qeshm Island, and two tankers reportedly caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz amid escalating tensions. Washington described the strikes as defensive, while Iran's IRGC confirmed the tanker incidents.

events.headline: Indonesia Sacks Presidential Chief of Staff and Detains Police Generals Over Wiretapping Scandal
events.summary: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto dismissed his chief of staff and authorities detained several police generals over allegations of illegally wiretapping the president. The scandal has deepened scrutiny of Indonesia's security apparatus.

events.headline: Mississippi US Senate Race Uncalled; Democrat Colom Leads Hyde-Smith by About 1,100 Votes
events.summary: Democratic challenger Scott Colom held a roughly 1,100-vote lead over incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith as of November 5, with Mississippi's U.S. Senate race still too close to call. A Colom win would make him the first Black senator from Mississippi since Reconstruction.

events.headline: Polish President Nawrocki Confronts Judges as Riot Police Deployed in Court Standoff
events.summary: Poland's constitutional crisis escalated as President Karol Nawrocki had a physical confrontation with judges at the Constitutional Tribunal, prompting deployment of riot police. The standoff between Nawrocki and the Tusk government has already triggered the resignation of three Polish ambassadors.

events.headline: Keisha Lance Bottoms Wins Georgia Governor's Race, First Black Woman to Hold the Office
events.summary: Former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms (D) defeated Republican Rick Jackson 54.3%-45.7% to become Georgia's first Black woman governor and the state's first Democratic governor since 1998. Democrats also flipped the state House, positioning Carolyn Hugley to become its first Black woman speaker.

events.headline: Al-Shabaab Claims Mass-Casualty Ambush on Somali Convoy in Lower Shabelle
events.summary: On Oct 26-27, 2026, al-Shabaab ambushed a Somali government/allied-militia convoy near Leego, Lower Shabelle region, during Operation Banooda, using explosive-laden vehicles; al-Shabaab claims it killed over 300 troops, while Somali officials counter it was a major assault by government forces. The death toll is independently unconfirmed, but analysts call it the army's worst setback since 2023.

events.headline: Amy Acton Defeats Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio Governor's Race, Becomes First Woman Elected Governor
events.summary: Democrat Amy Acton defeated Republican Vivek Ramaswamy 52.0%-44.7% in Ohio's previously undecided governor's race, becoming the first woman elected governor of Ohio and the first Democrat elected to the post in two decades.

events.headline: Alan Wilson Elected South Carolina Governor; Democrat Annie Andrews Wins US Senate Seat
events.summary: Republican Alan Wilson won South Carolina's open governor's race with 51.6% of the vote, succeeding term-limited Gov. Henry McMaster as the state's first new governor in over a decade. Separately, Democrat Dr. Annie Andrews defeated interim GOP Sen. Darline Graham 51.1%-46.7%, becoming the first woman and Democrat elected to the U.S. Senate from South Carolina in decades, as state Democrats also flipped 10 House seats to break the GOP supermajority.

events.headline: Mandatory Evacuations in Pagosa Springs, Colorado, as San Juan River Nears Record Crest
events.summary: A second storm wave triggered mandatory evacuations in Archuleta County, Colorado, as the San Juan River rose to 16.8 feet/11,200 cfs — the second-highest stage on record, just below the historic 1911 mark of 17.8 feet. Highway 160 closed, Red Cross shelters opened, and the Colorado National Guard deployed.

events.headline: Jocelyn Benson Elected Michigan Governor; Abdul El-Sayed Wins US Senate Seat
events.summary: Democratic Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson defeated Republican Rep. John James by roughly 11 points to win Michigan's governor's race on November 3. Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers by about 7 points for Michigan's open U.S. Senate seat, becoming the nation's first Muslim U.S. senator.

events.headline: Federal Judge Rejects DOJ Bid to Segregate About 20,000 'Likely Non-Citizen' California Ballots
events.summary: A federal judge denied a DOJ emergency request to force California to segregate roughly 20,000 ballots the department claims belong to likely non-citizens, two days before the Nov. 3 election, ruling it would "wreak havoc" on the vote. An appeals panel also rejected a similar request.

events.headline: US to Host Russia-Ukraine Trilateral Talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11
events.summary: US officials Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will lead trilateral talks with Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11, reviving a diplomatic track on post-war security arrangements that had been suspended since February.

events.headline: Byron Donalds Elected Florida Governor, First Black Republican Governor in US History
events.summary: Trump-backed Rep. Byron Donalds (R) narrowly defeated Democrat David Jolly, roughly 50.0% to 48.5%, to win Florida's open governor's race on November 3. Donalds, who succeeds term-limited Gov. Ron DeSantis, becomes the first elected Black Republican governor in U.S. history.

events.headline: Texas Flips: Democrat Gina Hinojosa Elected Governor, Ousting Greg Abbott
events.summary: Democratic state Rep. Gina Hinojosa defeated incumbent Gov. Greg Abbott, becoming Texas's first Democratic governor since the 1990s and its first Hispanic governor. The same night, Democrat James Talarico defeated Sen. Ken Paxton for US Senate, Texas's first Democratic Senate win since 1988, and Vikki Goodwin unseated 10-year incumbent Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick.

events.headline: UN Investigation Finds Hallmarks of Genocide in El Fasher One Year After RSF Takeover
events.summary: A UN fact-finding mission concluded that mass killings, gang rapes and deliberate starvation by the RSF in El Fasher, North Darfur, constitute "the hallmarks of genocide." One year after the city's October 2025 capture, North Darfur's governor alleges RSF forces committed 320 gang-rape cases at El Fasher University and 140 mass graves have been identified; Amnesty International's October 2026 follow-up found ongoing unlawful killings, detention, starvation and torture of civilians.

events.headline: Nearly 6 Million Face Acute Hunger in Haiti Amid Gang Violence and El Nino Drought
events.summary: The UN estimates nearly 5.94 million Haitians face acute food insecurity, a figure projected to rise to 6.35 million by mid-2027, driven by gang violence and El Nino-linked drought. Separately, the UN human rights office reports more than 5,700 people killed or wounded by gang violence between January and mid-September, including over 1,000 rapes and 230 kidnappings.

events.headline: Historic Flash Flooding Triggers Mass Evacuations in Sedona, Arizona
events.summary: A second Pacific storm dumped up to 4 inches of rain across the Southwest on Nov. 1-2, triggering mandatory evacuations in Sedona zones near Oak Creek and prompting water rescues. The same system caused severe flooding in southern Colorado, where Gov. Polis issued a disaster declaration.

events.headline: Palisades Fire Arson Retrial Begins in Los Angeles Federal Court
events.summary: Jury selection began Nov. 2 in the federal retrial of Jonathan Rinderknecht, who is accused of igniting the Palisades Fire. His first trial ended in a hung jury in June 2026.

events.headline: David Crowley Becomes Wisconsin's First Black Governor as Democrats Win Full Trifecta
events.summary: Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley (D) defeated Rep. Tom Tiffany (R) 53.4%-46.6% to become Wisconsin's first Black governor. Democrats also flipped both the state Senate and Assembly, securing a full Democratic trifecta for the first time since 2010.

events.headline: Learjet Crashes Near Greenacres, Florida, Killing All 9 Aboard
events.summary: A Learjet 60 flying from Austin, Texas, to North Eleuthera, Bahamas, crashed near a residential area in Greenacres, Florida, around 12:50 p.m. on Nov. 1, killing all nine people aboard. Gov. Ron DeSantis called the crash "cataclysmic."

events.headline: RSF Drone Strikes Push Sudan's Power Grid Toward Collapse
events.summary: Rapid Support Forces drones have struck 15-18 power stations across Sudan since early October, including the 500-megawatt Um Dabakir plant on Oct 29, cutting White Nile and North Kordofan states off the national grid. The campaign threatens to collapse what remains of Sudan's electricity infrastructure amid the ongoing civil war.

events.headline: Oregon's 2026 Wildfire Season Becomes Largest on Record, Nearly 2 Million Acres Burned
events.summary: Oregon's 2026 wildfire season burned roughly 2 to 2.3 million acres, surpassing the prior record of about 1.93 million acres set in 2024, at a suppression cost near $1.4 billion. FEMA reversed an earlier denial of federal fire-management assistance for the Rowe Creek Complex fire after appeals from Oregon lawmakers.

events.headline: Deb Haaland Elected New Mexico Governor, First Native American Woman to Lead a US State
events.summary: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland defeated Republican Rio Rancho Mayor Gregg Hull by roughly 57%-43% to become New Mexico's governor. Haaland is the first Native American woman elected to lead any US state.

events.headline: Germany's 'GenZ Regelt' Protests Turn Violent, New Mobilization Planned for Nov 14
events.summary: Protests and arrests continued across Frankfurt and other German cities following violent 'GenZ Regelt' demonstrations over education and military service policy. Organizers have called for a new nationwide mobilization on November 14.

events.headline: US Formally Removes South Africa and Rwanda From AGOA Trade Program
events.summary: The Trump administration confirmed it is cutting South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) trade program. The move will strip both countries of preferential US market access and comes amid broader diplomatic friction.

events.headline: US Military Boat-Strike Campaign Continues; Cumulative Drug-Boat Death Toll Tops 240
events.summary: The US military carried out additional strikes on suspected drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific, pushing the cumulative death toll from the campaign past 240. The strikes continue a controversial campaign that has drawn criticism over its legality and lack of transparency.

events.headline: North Korea Test-Fires New Air-Defense and Cruise Missiles Near Sondok
events.summary: North Korea's state media said it test-fired a new air-defense missile system and cruise missiles in drills near Sondok, South Hamgyong province. The tests are the latest in a series of weapons demonstrations toward the East Sea.
events.locationName: Sondok, South Hamgyong Province, North Korea

events.headline: South Africa's Local Elections Show Tight ANC-DA Race in Early Results
events.summary: Early results from South Africa's nationwide local government elections show the ANC leading with about 32% of the vote against the DA's 31%, with partial counting completed. The tight race signals continued erosion of the ANC's traditional dominance.

events.headline: South Korea's Kospi Extends Plunge as Chip Stock Selloff Spreads Across Asia
events.summary: South Korea's Kospi index extended a sharp decline of over 3% as chip stocks tumbled on AI valuation fears, with the selloff rippling across other Asian markets. Investors are increasingly rotating out of semiconductor and AI-linked equities.

events.headline: UN Rapporteur Calls Myanmar's Human Rights Situation 'Catastrophic' Amid Junta Attacks on Civilians
events.summary: A UN Special Rapporteur described Myanmar's human rights situation as catastrophic, saying the junta is attacking civilians to terrorize them while continuing arms purchases to fuel the war. The statement follows junta airstrikes that killed children at a school in Karenni State and bombed villages in Rakhine.

events.headline: Learjet 60 Crash in Florida Kills All 9 Aboard; NTSB Cites In-Flight Breakup
events.summary: A Learjet 60 crashed near Palm Beach, Florida, killing all nine people aboard. US transportation officials and the NTSB said the aircraft suffered an in-flight structural breakup before impact.

events.headline: Kansas Governor's Race Still Uncalled; Democrat Holscher Claims Victory, Mandatory Audit Triggered
events.summary: Democrat Cindy Holscher declared victory over Republican Senate President Ty Masterson in Kansas's governor's race, with her lead growing to roughly 7,045 votes (about 50.3%-49.7%). Masterson has not conceded, and the narrow margin triggers a state-mandated close-race audit.

events.headline: Localized Ceasefire Collapses in Ukraine's Kherson Region, Russia Resumes Attacks
events.summary: A localized ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region ended, and Russian forces resumed attacks on the area, prompting fresh civilian evacuations near Oleshky. Kyiv said the truce's collapse underscores the fragility of regional de-escalation efforts.

events.headline: Brazil Summons Argentine Envoy Over Flávio Bolsonaro's Escape to US via Argentina
events.summary: Brazil formally summoned Argentina's diplomatic representative after Flávio Bolsonaro fled to the United States via Argentine territory. Brasília is seeking clarification on how the transit was permitted.

events.headline: Colombia: Explosives Seized Near Nariño Toll Road, Drone Attacks Hit Police in Cauca and Chocó
events.summary: Colombian authorities seized 78 kilograms of explosives near a toll station on the Pan-American Highway in Nariño, foiling a suspected attack. Separately, armed groups carried out drone attacks on police in Cauca and Chocó departments amid a deepening displacement crisis.

events.headline: Pakistan Launches Counter-Strikes on Afghan Taliban Border Posts in South Waziristan
events.summary: Pakistani forces struck Afghan Taliban border posts in South Waziristan in response to what officials called unprovoked cross-border firing. The clash escalates tensions beyond the diplomatic track, even as Pakistan continues pressing the Taliban over the TTP with US mediation offered.

events.headline: Pritzker Wins Historic Third Term as Illinois Governor; Stratton Wins Open US Senate Seat
events.summary: Gov. JB Pritzker (D) defeated Darren Bailey roughly 60%-37% to become the first Illinois governor elected to a third term. Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton defeated Don Tracy for the Senate seat vacated by retiring Sen. Dick Durbin, becoming the second Black woman to serve Illinois in the U.S. Senate.

events.headline: Zelensky Presses Berlin for Faster Patriot Missile Deliveries
events.summary: Visiting Berlin for air-defense talks, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told German officials Ukraine faces a chronic shortage of Patriot interceptors and pressed for faster deliveries from Chancellor Merz's government.

events.headline: Poland Says It Blocked Overnight Sabotage Provocation Near Kaliningrad Border
events.summary: Polish authorities said they blocked an overnight provocation involving individuals using flashlights near the border with Russia's Kaliningrad exclave, who withdrew before being intercepted. The incident follows Poland's deployment of counter-terrorism police to the region over sabotage warnings.

events.headline: China Conducts Record Surge in Military Activity Around Taiwan
events.summary: Taiwan's defense ministry reported a record daily surge in Chinese military activity around the island, including 49 aircraft, six warships and six government vessels. The surge marks one of the largest single-day shows of force in recent months.

events.headline: Argentina's Economy Edges Toward Recession as Country-Risk Index Hits Highest in Over a Year
events.summary: Argentina's country-risk index surpassed 800 points, its highest level in more than a year, as austerity measures strain the economy. The downturn poses a political test for President Javier Milei ahead of the 2027 vote.

events.headline: Eurozone Inflation Jumps to 4% in October, Highest in Years
events.summary: Eurozone annual inflation rose to 4% in October, according to Eurostat data, marking a sharp acceleration that could pressure the European Central Bank's policy stance. Several member states saw particularly steep price jumps.

events.headline: EUFOR Chinook Helicopter Crash Near Brčko, Bosnia and Herzegovina Kills Four
events.summary: An Italian military Chinook helicopter serving with the EU peacekeeping force EUFOR crashed near Brčko, Bosnia and Herzegovina, killing four crew members. The cause of the crash is under investigation.

events.headline: Republican Mike Mazzei Wins Oklahoma Governor's Race as Democrats Flip 6 House Seats
events.summary: Republican Mike Mazzei defeated Democratic House Minority Leader Cyndi Munson 51.9%-45.9% to win Oklahoma's governor's race. Democrats flipped six GOP-held state House seats, their largest legislative gain in two decades, though Republicans retain their supermajority.

events.headline: New York State Reports First Measles Death in Over 30 Years
events.summary: Health officials in Lewis County, New York, confirmed the state's first measles-associated death in more than three decades. The case has intensified concern over declining vaccination rates in the US.
events.locationName: Lewis County, New York, United States

events.headline: Julia Letlow Becomes First Republican Woman Elected to US Senate From Louisiana
events.summary: Rep. Julia Letlow (R) narrowly defeated Democrat Jamie Davis 51%-49% for Louisiana's open U.S. Senate seat, becoming the first Republican woman elected to the Senate from Louisiana. Her vacated 5th Congressional District seat now heads to a December 12 runoff between Democrat Pat Moore and Republican Gabe Firment.

events.headline: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (D) Elected Alaska Governor, Flipping Governor's Seat
events.summary: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, won Alaska's governor's race with 49.1% of the vote, defeating Republican Bernadette Wilson's 29.2%, becoming the state's first Democratic governor since 2002 and its youngest ever. A ballot measure imposing a citizenship-only voting requirement was passing with roughly 70% support.

events.headline: Taiwan Tightens Military Draft Exemption Rules Amid Rising Tensions With China
events.summary: Taiwan has altered its draft exemption rules to add thousands more personnel to its armed forces, as China conducts a record surge in military activity around the island. The policy shift reflects growing concern over cross-strait tensions.

events.headline: Democrat Hannah Pingree Elected Maine Governor
events.summary: Democrat Hannah Pingree, Maine's former House speaker, won the state's open governor's race on November 3, defeating Republican Bobby Charles and independent Rick Bennett roughly 55% to 37% to 8%. She succeeds term-limited Gov. Janet Mills in January 2027.

events.headline: Josh Shapiro Re-elected Pennsylvania Governor in Landslide Over Stacy Garrity
events.summary: Gov. Josh Shapiro (D) defeated Republican state Treasurer Stacy Garrity by a wide margin, roughly 60%-37%, despite a Trump endorsement for Garrity. The decisive win cements Shapiro as a prominent national Democratic figure heading into his second term.

events.headline: Xavier Becerra Elected California Governor, First Latino Governor in Over 150 Years
events.summary: Democrat Xavier Becerra defeated Republican Steve Hilton by a wide margin, roughly 64%-36%, to become California's next governor. Becerra is the state's first Latino governor in more than 150 years.

events.headline: Israel's President Herzog Opens Coalition Talks After Accepting Election Results
events.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog accepted the results of recent elections and opened talks on forming a new government. Reports indicate former military chief Gadi Eisenkot is leading in endorsements to form the coalition.

events.headline: Ethiopia Expels Sudanese Diplomats Over RSF Support Allegations
events.summary: Ethiopia expelled Sudanese diplomats from Addis Ababa after fresh allegations that Sudanese officials supported the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. The move adds diplomatic strain amid Sudan's ongoing civil war.

events.headline: Ukrainian Drones Strike Russia's Slavneft-YANOS Oil Refinery in Yaroslavl
events.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Slavneft-YANOS oil refinery in Yaroslavl, Russia, triggering fires and power outages felt as far as occupied Crimea. The attack is part of Ukraine's intensified campaign against Russian energy infrastructure.

events.headline: Tommy Tuberville Elected Alabama Governor; Republicans Retain Open US Senate Seat
events.summary: Sen. Tommy Tuberville (R) defeated Democrat Doug Jones 52%-48% to become Alabama's governor. Republican Rep. Barry Moore won the open U.S. Senate seat Tuberville vacated, defeating Democrat Everett Wess roughly 54%-45%, meaning Republicans retained the seat.

events.headline: Cartel Violence Kills Seven, Including US Citizen Child, After Gulf Cartel Lieutenant's Arrest
events.summary: Violence erupted in Matamoros, Mexico after the arrest of a senior Gulf Cartel lieutenant, leaving seven people dead including a US citizen child. Mexican authorities deployed roughly 450 additional troops to the border city to restore order.

events.headline: Serbia Detains Senior Police Officials Over Torture and Abuse-of-Office Allegations
events.summary: Serbian authorities detained several senior police officials, including a police chief, on allegations of torture and abuse of office. The arrests come amid continued political turmoil in Serbia following recent elections.

events.headline: Record Flash Flooding on Toccoa River Triggers Rescues, Evacuations in North Georgia
events.summary: Torrential overnight rain sent the Toccoa River to a record crest early November 5, triggering what officials called a catastrophic flood event in McCaysville and surrounding north Georgia and southern Tennessee communities. Roughly 30 water rescues were conducted, schools closed, an emergency shelter opened, and a state of emergency was declared.

events.headline: Yemeni Government Forces Advance in Al-Jawf Under 'Operation Dawn of Yemen'
events.summary: Yemeni government forces seized strategic positions in Al-Jawf governorate as part of 'Operation Dawn of Yemen,' while the Saudi-led coalition intercepted a Houthi missile amid intensifying fighting. Yemeni forces reported over 1,200 strikes on Houthi positions in 24 hours.

events.headline: Democrat Aaron Ford Elected Nevada Governor as Democrats Sweep Statewide Offices
events.summary: Democratic Attorney General Aaron Ford defeated Republican incumbent Gov. Joe Lombardo to become Nevada's first Black governor. Democrats also won lieutenant governor, attorney general and treasurer, and held secretary of state, marking a full statewide sweep for the first time in decades.

events.headline: Nigeria's State Police Bill Sent to Tinubu Amid $7.7 Billion Loan Request
events.summary: Nigeria's National Assembly has sent a bill establishing state police forces to President Tinubu for assent, a major decentralization reform. The move coincides with a government request for $7.7 billion in new borrowing.

events.headline: Phil Scott Wins Record 6th Term as Vermont Governor Amid Democratic Legislative Gains
events.summary: Republican Gov. Phil Scott won a record sixth term on November 3, defeating Democrat Amanda Janoo roughly 52%-45%. Vermont Democrats simultaneously regained veto-proof supermajorities in both legislative chambers.

events.headline: Missouri Democrats Break GOP Supermajority; Voters Reject Abortion Rollback, Pass Amendment 6
events.summary: Missouri Democrats flipped 16 state House seats, their largest gain since 1974, ending the Republican legislative supermajority though the GOP retains a 95-68 majority. Voters also rejected Amendment 3, which would have rolled back 2024 abortion-rights protections, and approved Amendment 6, requiring an 80% supermajority to alter voter-approved ballot measures.

events.headline: Sarah Huckabee Sanders Wins Re-Election as Arkansas Governor
events.summary: Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders (R) won a second term on November 3, defeating Democrat Fred Love 53.9%-38.6% and Libertarian Colt Shelby 7.5%, as Republicans swept Arkansas's statewide offices.

events.headline: Whistleblower Alleges Sanctioned Russian Firm Secretly Financed Alaska Gas Project
events.summary: Former Polar LNG CEO Joel Riddle told the New York Times he resigned after discovering Russian energy giant Novatek, partially sanctioned over the Ukraine war, was financing and directing an Alaska North Slope gas export project despite being told funding came from a UAE firm. The allegations could trigger a US Treasury sanctions probe into the Trump-administration-linked deal; Polar LNG calls the claims unfounded and says it is investigating.

events.headline: RSF Claims Capture of Sali Military Base in Sudan's Blue Nile State
events.summary: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces and allied rebels claim to have captured the Sali military base in Blue Nile state, though the Sudanese army says it repelled the attack and inflicted heavy losses. The contested claim marks a new flashpoint in the civil war.

events.headline: Storm Agneta Triggers Severe Flooding in Rhodes, Greece, With Alerts Extending to Spain
events.summary: Storm Agneta brought severe flooding to Rhodes and other parts of Greece, damaging dozens of vehicles, while red-alert weather warnings were also issued in parts of Spain. Authorities warned the storm system would continue moving across the eastern Mediterranean.

events.headline: Syria and Saudi Arabia Sign Defense Pact and $403 Million Loan Deal
events.summary: Syria's interim president Ahmed al-Sharaa visited Riyadh, where Syrian and Saudi defense ministries signed a cooperation agreement and Saudi Arabia pledged $403 million in loans. The deal underscores Gulf states' growing engagement with Syria's post-war government.

events.headline: Mexico's Electoral Authority Crisis Deepens Amid Corruption Allegations and Asset Freezes
events.summary: The head of Mexico's electoral institute (INE) resigned amid corruption allegations, deepening a crisis at the body ahead of upcoming votes. Authorities have also frozen assets linked to the investigation.

events.headline: Utah Legislature Sees Democratic Gains; Ben McAdams Wins Back US House Seat
events.summary: Early results showed roughly 15 Democratic and unaffiliated challengers leading or defeating Republican state legislative incumbents in historically GOP-dominated Utah. Democrat Ben McAdams won Utah's 1st Congressional District, and voters passed Amendment A removing newspaper-publication requirements from the state constitution while rejecting Amendment B, which would have raised the threshold for tax-related ballot initiatives.

events.headline: US, NATO and World Bank Convene Brussels Summit on Ukraine Reconstruction
events.summary: European countries, the US, NATO and the World Bank convened in Brussels for a summit on Ukraine's reconstruction. The gathering comes as planning intensifies for postwar rebuilding alongside separate trilateral peace talks.

events.headline: Houthi Attack on Yemeni Government Training Camp Kills Dozens in Qataba
events.summary: A Houthi missile attack struck a Yemeni government military training camp in Qataba, al-Dhale'e governorate, killing dozens of recruits. The attack marks a significant escalation on a front separate from the government's ongoing Al-Jawf offensive.

events.headline: Tanzania Sets November 6 Verdict Date in Opposition Leader Lissu's Treason Trial
events.summary: A Tanzanian court has scheduled November 6 for the verdict in the treason trial of opposition leader Tundu Lissu. The case has drawn international scrutiny over the state of political freedoms ahead of the ruling.

events.headline: Suspected Bandits Abduct 14 Islamic School Pupils and Teacher in Nigeria's Niger State
events.summary: Armed bandits abducted 14 pupils and a teacher from an Islamic school in Tungan-Bako, Niger State, Nigeria, police confirmed. The kidnapping is part of a continuing wave of mass abductions targeting schools in the region.

events.headline: Bank of Japan Minutes Show Debate Over Further Rate Hikes
events.summary: Minutes from the Bank of Japan's September meeting show policymakers debated the need for further interest rate hikes and discussed scope for faster moves, after rates reached 1.25%. The minutes offer insight into the BOJ's tightening trajectory.

events.headline: Wall Street Surges and Oil Prices Tumble on Election Results and Iran De-escalation Hopes
events.summary: The Dow Jones jumped roughly 1,500 points (3%) following the US midterm results while Brent crude fell more than 10% below $100 a barrel on hopes of easing US-Iran tensions. Analysts linked the rally to political clarity and reduced fears of a wider Gulf conflict.

events.headline: New Jersey Governor Warns Ports Against Accepting Russian Diesel Shipments
events.summary: Gov. Mikie Sherrill sent letters to roughly a dozen New Jersey port and terminal operators warning them to turn away tankers carrying Russian diesel, arguing a recent Treasury license conflicts with the 2022 federal ban on Russian oil-product imports. She warned operators could face civil or criminal penalties for accepting the shipments.

events.headline: Taiwan Accuses China of APEC Protocol Violation Over Emailed Shenzhen Summit Invitation
events.summary: Taiwan accused China of violating APEC protocol by sending an emailed invitation to a Shenzhen summit in a manner Taipei said was designed to diminish its status. The dispute adds to ongoing friction between Taiwan and China over diplomatic recognition.

events.headline: NSW Health Declares 'Major Incident' Over Cyber Breach, Launches Criminal Investigation
events.summary: New South Wales Health declared a major incident after a cyber breach exposed sensitive data, prompting a criminal investigation into suspected overseas hackers. Authorities are working to assess the scope of compromised patient records.

events.headline: Nationwide Strike Paralyzes France's Transport and Schools
events.summary: A nationwide strike including SNCF rail workers disrupted transport and schools across France on November 5, following days of student blockades. Unions are protesting pension and labor policy, with major cities bracing for mass mobilization.

events.headline: Israeli Forces Kill Six Militants in Khan Younis Despite Gaza Ceasefire
events.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet said they killed six militants in an operation in Khan Younis, the latest in a series of lethal incidents in Gaza despite the ceasefire agreement. Palestinian officials continue to report casualties in the area.

events.headline: Five Charged in $235 Million Fraud Scheme Targeting Australia's NDIS and Welfare Payments
events.summary: Australian Federal Police charged five people over an alleged $235 million fraud scheme targeting the National Disability Insurance Scheme, childcare subsidies and veterans' payments. The operation highlights ongoing concerns about fraud within Australia's welfare system.

events.headline: Libya's Eastern Parliament Appoints Fawzi Abu Khazam as New Central Bank Governor
events.summary: Libya's eastern-based parliament appointed Fawzi Abu Khazam as the new governor of the central bank, accepting the resignation of his predecessor. The move caps a series of recent changes to Libya's financial leadership amid ongoing political division between eastern and western authorities.

events.headline: Grizzly Bear Attack Kills Mother and Daughter in British Columbia
events.summary: A mother and daughter were killed in a suspected grizzly bear attack near Bella Coola, British Columbia. Canadian wildlife authorities tracked and dealt with multiple grizzlies in the area following the incident.

events.headline: EU's Kallas Says 'Everything on the Table' for New Measures Against Georgia
events.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the bloc will discuss new measures against Georgia's government in January, citing democratic backsliding. The remarks came after an EU Foreign Affairs Council meeting in Brussels.

events.headline: China's Central Bank Shifts Main Policy Rate to Boost Real Economy
events.summary: China's central bank (PBOC) is shifting its main policy rate to the overnight reverse repo rate as part of a broader monetary framework overhaul aimed at supporting banks and boosting the real economy.

events.headline: Wyoming Voters Reject Property-Tax Cut Proposition 1 as Eric Barlow Wins Governor's Race
events.summary: Republican Eric Barlow won Wyoming's open governor's race with 68.6% of the vote, succeeding term-limited Gov. Mark Gordon. Voters separately rejected Proposition 1, a proposed 50% cut to residential property taxes, by roughly 57%-43%.

events.headline: Gov. Josh Green Wins Landslide Re-Election; Green Party Makes History in Hawaii Legislature
events.summary: Gov. Josh Green (D) won re-election in a landslide, defeating Republican Gary Cordery with about 74% of the vote. In West Maui, Green Party candidate Pa'ele Kiakona unseated Democratic incumbent Rep. Elle Cochran by 107 votes, becoming the first third-party candidate elected to Hawaii's Legislature since statehood.

events.headline: Bomb Threats Disrupt Multiple Flights Across Poland, Spain and Bulgaria
events.summary: A wave of bomb threats forced the evacuation and diversion of several flights across Europe, including in Warsaw, Spain and Bulgaria. No explosives were found, and authorities are investigating the source of the coordinated threats.

events.headline: Wes Moore Wins Second Term as Maryland Governor in Landslide
events.summary: Democrat Wes Moore defeated Republican Dan Cox by about 29 points, roughly 62.6%-33%, in a rematch of their 2022 race; Lt. Gov. Aruna Miller was also re-elected. Moore now faces a projected $3 billion state budget shortfall in his second term.

events.headline: Bangladesh Garment Workers Continue Multi-Day Wage Protests; Government Forms Wage Board
events.summary: Garment workers in Bangladesh continued wage protests for a third consecutive day, disrupting factory operations in Dhaka and Gazipur. The government responded by announcing the formation of a wage board to address worker demands.

events.headline: Helena Foulkes Wins Rhode Island Governor's Race; Voters Reject Two Bond Measures
events.summary: Democrat Helena Foulkes won Rhode Island's governorship in a landslide on November 3, defeating independent Ken Block and Republican Aaron Guckian. Voters approved $450 million in bonds but rejected two of five bond questions worth $150 million, the state's first bond rejection in 20 years.

events.headline: Amy Klobuchar Elected Minnesota's First Female Governor
events.summary: US Sen. Amy Klobuchar (D) defeated Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth (R) roughly 57%-43% in the open-seat race after Gov. Tim Walz declined to seek a third term. Klobuchar becomes Minnesota's first female governor.

events.headline: Canada and US Signal Progress in Trade Deal Talks
events.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said negotiators have made progress toward a new Canada-US trade agreement, as talks continued in the shadow of the US midterm elections. Both sides indicated a deal could ease ongoing tariff disputes.

events.headline: Armenia Says Ready to Sign Peace Treaty With Azerbaijan Amid Domestic Political Tensions
events.summary: Armenia's foreign minister said Yerevan is ready to sign a peace treaty with Azerbaijan as early as this year. The statement comes as Prime Minister Pashinyan accuses Russia-linked circles of backing an opposition plot amid unrest in parliament.

events.headline: Fiji Military Formally Backs Removing Constitutional Coup-Immunity Provisions
events.summary: Fiji's military formally declared its support for removing coup-immunity provisions from the constitution, pledging political neutrality. The move comes as Fiji's parliament has delayed a vote on the constitutional amendment bill to December.

events.headline: Marsha Blackburn Elected Tennessee's First Woman Governor
events.summary: US Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R) won a narrower-than-expected race over Democrat Jerri Green to become Tennessee's first female governor. Voters also approved amendments expanding courts' ability to deny bail in certain violent-crime cases and permanently banning a state property tax.

events.headline: Seven Arrested in Cross-Border Investment-Fraud Crackdown Across Kosovo, Albania and North Macedonia
events.summary: Authorities across Kosovo, Albania and North Macedonia, coordinated by Eurojust, dismantled an international investment-fraud scheme and arrested seven people. Servers used to run the scheme were also seized.

events.headline: Egypt and Sudan Reaffirm Defense and Water-Security Pact, Reject Unilateral GERD Actions
events.summary: Egypt and Sudan reaffirmed a defense and water-security agreement, jointly rejecting unilateral actions in the Eastern Nile Basin related to the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam. The agreement underscores deepening cooperation between Cairo and Khartoum amid regional tensions over the Nile.

events.headline: Egypt Signs $1 Billion World Bank Financing Agreement for Economic Reform Program
events.summary: Egypt signed a $1 billion financing agreement with the World Bank to support the second phase of its economic reform program. The deal comes as Egypt pursues broader fiscal stabilization measures.

events.headline: Lithium-Ion Batteries Named Cause of Fatal Boston Firefighter Fire
events.summary: Boston Fire Commissioner Rodney Marshall announced on November 4 that lithium-ion batteries stored in plastic toolboxes on a Dorchester porch underwent thermal runaway, sparking the May 23, 2026 Treadway Road fire that killed firefighter Robert 'Bobby' Kilduff Jr. The announcement concludes the department's investigation into the fatal fire.

events.headline: Washington Voters Reject Repeal of 'Millionaires Tax' on High Incomes
events.summary: Washington voters rejected Initiative 645, which would have repealed the state's 9.9% tax on income above $1 million, by roughly 58%-42%. A separate constitutional challenge to the tax, Petter v. Washington, remains pending in Klickitat County Superior Court.

events.headline: EU Enlargement Report Names Montenegro Frontrunner for Membership
events.summary: The European Commission's 2026 enlargement report praised reform progress across candidate countries, naming Montenegro the current frontrunner for EU membership. The report urges deeper reforms across the Western Balkans.

events.headline: China Showcases 6G Prototype Tech at Shanghai Import Expo
events.summary: At the 9th China International Import Expo in Shanghai, Qualcomm demonstrated 6G smart-glasses prototype technology, part of a broader showcase of next-generation wireless and consumer tech from global firms.

events.headline: Kyiv Independent Hit by Suspected Russian Cyberattack
events.summary: The Kyiv Independent news outlet was hit by a cyberattack suspected to be linked to Russia. The outlet's systems were disrupted, with cybersecurity researchers investigating the source of the intrusion.

events.headline: Trial Begins for Suspect in Deadly Leipzig Car-Ramming Attack
events.summary: The trial of the suspect accused of carrying out a deadly car-ramming attack in Leipzig, Germany, began this week. A judge had previously ordered the suspect to undergo psychiatric evaluation.

events.headline: Al-Shabaab Mortar Attack Kills Civilians Near Bosaso, Puntland
events.summary: An al-Shabaab mortar attack killed at least three civilians and wounded seven others near Galgala in Puntland, Somalia. The attack is separate from a recent large-scale al-Shabaab ambush in Lower Shabelle.

events.headline: Thailand Reaffirms Cambodia Border Will Stay Closed Indefinitely
events.summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said the border with Cambodia would remain closed indefinitely, ruling out a return to normal relations for now. The closure continues to disrupt cross-border trade and travel between the two countries.

events.headline: Cyclone Wati Strikes Cook Islands as Unusually Early First Named Storm of Season
events.summary: Tropical Cyclone Wati struck the Cook Islands, including Aitutaki, as the season's first named cyclone, forming unusually early. Authorities issued warnings as the system tracked south toward open waters.

events.headline: Delhi's Air Quality Deteriorates to 'Very Poor,' GRAP Stage II Curbs Invoked
events.summary: New Delhi's air quality worsened to 'very poor' levels, with the AQI climbing to 331, prompting authorities to invoke Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan. The curbs include restrictions aimed at controlling pollution sources across the capital region.

events.headline: Brazil's Central Bank Holds Selic Rate at 13.75%, Ending Run of Cuts
events.summary: Brazil's central bank (Copom) held its benchmark Selic interest rate at 13.75%, ending a recent cycle of rate cuts. The decision follows political developments after Lula's election win and comes amid pressure on Brazilian markets.

events.headline: Putin Marks National Unity Day With Remarks Denying Russia Poses Any Threat
events.summary: President Vladimir Putin marked Russia's National Unity Day by awarding state prizes and saying Russia has never threatened any country and poses no threat now. The remarks come amid ongoing fighting in Ukraine and Western sanctions pressure.

events.headline: Israeli Strike Kills Motorcyclist in Southern Lebanon
events.summary: An Israeli strike killed one person and wounded another on a motorcycle in Qabrikha, southern Lebanon. Lebanese officials said the strike is part of continued Israeli operations despite a broader regional ceasefire framework.

events.headline: Brazil's Ibovespa Stock Index Hits Six-Month Low Ahead of Selic Rate Decision
events.summary: Brazil's benchmark Ibovespa stock index fell to its lowest level in six months as investors positioned ahead of the central bank's upcoming Selic interest-rate decision. The decline reflects growing caution over inflation and fiscal policy in Latin America's largest economy.

events.headline: Drone Strike Hits Ozon Logistics Warehouse in Southern Russia's Adygeysk
events.summary: A drone strike hit a warehouse operated by Russian online retailer Ozon in the town of Adygeysk, in Russia's Republic of Adygea. The incident adds to a growing pattern of drone strikes on logistics and industrial infrastructure deep inside Russian territory.
